text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has asked for appropriate action to be taken to stop the illegal departure of Vietnamese to Hong Kong. Between January and October, 812 Vietnamese left illegally for Hong Kong. About 780 went by sea and the remainder were tourists who overstayed their visa.

-- State-owned enterprises must pay no less than three percent of their after-tax profit to the National Investment Promotion Fund, the Ministry of Finance said. Fifty percent of the fund's capital will come from the National Budget and mobilised capital and the rest will be raised from state enterprises.

-- Vietnam's President Le Duc Anh has reaffirmed Vietnam's unshakeable stance in supporting Palestine and the Palestine Liberation Organisation in their just cause to defend their national inviolable national rights.
-- Vietnam will be allowed to draw on another $88 million under the three-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility arrangement (ESAF) from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
-- The VietsovPetro joint venture expects turnover of $1.2 billion and crude oil output of 8.2 million tonnes in 1996.
-- Vietnam's consumer prices rose 0.9 percent in November from October.
-- Vietnam's government said there have been positive changes in industrial production in November, with output rising 16.7 compared with the same period last year.
-- Income tax for the public transport business will be reduced by at least 50 percent and there will be exemptions from other kinds of tax during the 1996-1997 period.
